newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 15.00 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 15.00 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs rose 158 basis points to 15.00 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.
The Central Bank said it sold 3.95 billion bolivars of 179-day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills out of the 40 billion bolivars offered.
The bills, which carried a 13.42 percent coupon, sold for 99.27 pct. At last week's auction, six-month notes yielded 13.42 percent.
Out of a total 20 billion bolivars of offered 268-day notes with a 13.64 percent coupon, the bank sold 10.24 billion bolivars worth at a price of 97.06 percent.
For 358-day notes carrying a 13.86 percent coupon, the bank sold 4.00 billion bolivars out of 20 billion bolivars on offer at an average price of 95.03 percent.
Yields on these notes rose 145 basis points to 18.13 percent for the 268-day bills, and 251 basis points to 19.84 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
